verbs.name: audio.add_music
verbs.description: Place an already-imported music asset as a BED under the timeline and (by default) AUTO-DUCK it under the base track's speech. Import the music first (media.import{path}); the import chain runs perception, so the asset's beat grid + silences are then available. The bed is placed on a dedicated audio track (auto-creates 'music1' when `track` is omitted) at `at_ms` (default 0) with `bed_gain_db` (default -18, the bed sits clearly under the VO). AUTO-DUCK reuses the edit.duck windowed-gain machinery: speech windows are computed NOW from the against-track's perception silences (default against = the base audio/speech track) and RECORDED on the op (deterministic, auditable — re-run after adding/moving speech; ripples remap them). Pass `duck:false` to skip ducking, or `duck:{against_track?, db?, attack_ms?}` to tune it (db default -15, attack_ms default 250). BEAT MARKERS (label 'beat', note 'beat:<index> bpm:<bpm>') are surfaced from the bed asset's perception beat grid, mapped to the bed's timeline position (mirrors the capture:* marker pattern) — pass beat_markers:false to skip. Lowers to real edit ops (add_track? + insert{ripple:false} + gain + duck + per-beat add_marker), recorded so replay reproduces them while the op keeps the name audio.add_music. INTERACTION: ducking is windowed gain, NOT a render-time sidechain (cut_core::GainWindow); composes with edit.fade on the bed (fade the bed in/out independently) and renders through the same amix as any audio track.

track.description: Existing audio track for the bed; omit to use/create 'music1'

at_ms.description: Timeline position for the bed start; default 0

src_range_ms.description: Sub-range of the music asset to use; default the full asset

bed_gain_db.description: Bed level in dB; default -18 (under the VO)

duck.description: Auto-duck config, or false to skip. Object: {against_track?: string (default base audio track), db?: number (negative, default -15), attack_ms?: integer (default 250)}. Omitted = auto-duck with defaults.

beat_markers.description: Surface beat:<index> markers from the bed asset's perception beat grid (default true)

fit_to_timeline.description: Trim the bed to the current timeline length so it sits UNDER the video instead of extending it with trailing black/silence (only shortens; ignored if src_range_ms is given). Default false = full asset.

include_inverse.description: Deprecated compatibility option. Accepted for v0.6 callers but new operations use recompute-by-replay and have no inverse payload to include.

verbs.result: {track_id, bed_clip, bed_gain_db, bed_duration_ms, ducked_windows, beats_marked, created_track, op} — one audio.add_music op appended (lowering edit.add_track?/insert/gain/duck/add_marker steps)

verbs.name: audio.dub
verbs.description: Native AI DUBBING: re-voice an asset's speech into target_lang in a cloned `voice` (default "rebeka"), TIME-FIT to the original, and ADD it as a NEW audio track at the original segment timings. The ORIGINAL audio is KEPT (a mutable mix) — dubbing ADDS a track, it never replaces. Pipeline: read the asset's word-level transcript (it MUST be transcribed — media.transcribe first) → group into sentence-ish segments → TRANSLATE each segment into target_lang (REUSES the transcript.translate machinery: PRIMARY = the user's subscription CLI agent claude/codex/grok; FALLBACK = the local Opus-MT/MADLAD sidecar) → SYNTHESIZE each translated segment via the OmniVoice TTS service (dub_runner.py POSTs each with `duration` = the segment's [start,end] slot length, then `atempo`-trims the residual to hit the slot, and assembles ONE continuous 24 kHz mono WAV with each segment placed at its ORIGINAL start time, silence between) → IMPORT the WAV as an asset → place it as per-segment clips on a fresh `dub<N>` audio track (op-log, replay-safe; ripple:false so the dub floats and nothing shifts). The network touch (translate + synth) happens BEFORE the op is recorded, so a service failure fails the verb cleanly (never a fake/empty track) and replay/render stay OFFLINE. The TTS endpoint is CUT_DUB_ENDPOINT (default http://127.0.0.1:9001; set it before launch when the service uses a custom address). Voice-cloning a NEW speaker is an offline train job (out of scope here); this verb synthesizes with an EXISTING registered voice. Receipt (surfaced + written to receipts/<asset>.<lang>.dub.json): source_lang, target_lang, voice, model, n_segments, mean_fit_ratio, and per-segment {slot_ms, synth_ms, fit_ratio, placed_at_ms, placed_ms}.

asset.description: Asset whose speech to dub. Optional when exactly one asset has a transcript.

target_lang.description: Language to dub INTO (e.g. "lv", "es", "Latvian"). For the LOCAL translation backend a 2-letter code is required.

voice.description: TTS voice id (an existing registered OmniVoice voice, e.g. "rebeka"). Default "rebeka". Unknown voices error (the service lists registered voices).

source_lang.description: Source language. Optional for the CLI translation backend (the LLM auto-detects); REQUIRED for the local Opus-MT backend (per-pair). Defaults to the transcript's detected language.

backend.description: Translation backend: auto (default) = CLI if available else local; cli/local force one.

model.description: Override the TRANSLATION model: a CLI model name or a local HF id (e.g. a MADLAD-400 build). Default local = Opus-MT for the pair.

timeout_ms.description: Translation spawn timeout (CLI default 180000; local default 1800000). Synthesis has its own generous per-run budget.

verbs.result: {asset, track_id, dub_asset, dub_wav, source_lang, target_lang, voice, n_segments, n_clips, total_ms, sample_rate, mean_fit_ratio, translate_backend, translate_model, receipt, clips:[{i,at_ms,range_ms,slot_ms,fit_ratio}], op} — ONE audio.dub op appended (lowering edit.add_track + per-segment edit.insert{ripple:false}); the dubbed WAV is imported as its own media.import op. receipt = the relative path of receipts/<asset>.<lang>.dub.json.
